On Fri, Nov 20, 2015 at 6:51 PM, Mathias Tobler <mato...@gmail.com> wrote:

Sean,

three things.

1) in win.data your variable is Density and in your model the variable is density. The BUGS language is case sensitive so it does not recognize Density.

2) You can't have missing values in your independent variables (e.g. forest, density) unless you draw missing values from a distribution in your model. Missing values for y are not an issue. 50% missing values seems very high. You might want to first test your model without the missing values to make sure it runs well.

3) Use normal priors for your alpha and beta.

Hope that helps.

Mathias

Hi Sean,

Regarding imputing missing values for 'density' as Mathias noted: there are multiple ways to do this. One way is fixing density NA's equal to the mean of the observed density [i, j], and another is treating density [i, j] as a stochastic node: density[i, j]~dnorm(mu.obs.density, tau.obs.density), where mu.obs.density and tau.obs.density are the sample mean and precision of the observed data. The prior distribution for density in option 2 may not necessarily be normal, depending upon what the variable is: e.g., density[i, j]~dpois(lam.obs.density), or even estimating missing values as a function of yet additional covariates, etc.  There are probably several other ways to approach this as well.  Either way, it might be worth assessing sensitivity to different methods of dealing with missing values.   

Otherwise, is forest indexed correctly as forest[i,]?  It looks the data are a matrix (forest[i,] vs. forest[i]). 
 
One final thought: my memory is that there were some issues with R2JAGS (incorrect burn-in or something like that). I don't know if this has been fixed, but you might prefer to use 'jagsUI' or 'rjags'.  The former makes the running of chains in parallel very easy, which is a nice feature.

John
